13: 
14: ## Installation
15: 
16: To obtain the latest version, simply require the project using `npm`:
17: 
18: ```shell
19: npm install @ethereumjs/common
20: ```
21: 
22: ## Usage
23: 
24: ### import / require
25: 
26: import (ESM, TypeScript):
27: 
28: ```typescript
29: import { Chain, Common, Hardfork } from '@ethereumjs/common
30: ```
31: 
32: require (CommonJS, Node.js):
33: 
34: ```typescript
35: const { Common, Chain, Hardfork } = require('@ethereumjs/common')
36: ```
37: 
38: ## Parameters
39: 
40: All parameters can be accessed through the `Common` class, instantiated with an object containing either the `chain` (e.g. 'Chain.Mainnet') or the `chain` together with a specific `hardfork` provided:
41: 
42: ```typescript
43: // With enums:
44: const common = new Common({ chain: Chain.Mainnet, hardfork: Hardfork.London })
45: 
46: // (also possible with directly passing in strings:)
47: const common = new Common({ chain: 'mainnet', hardfork: 'london' })
48: ```
49: 
50: If no hardfork is provided, the common is initialized with the default hardfork.
51: 
52: Current `DEFAULT_HARDFORK`: `Hardfork.Merge`
53: 
54: Here are some simple usage examples:
55: 
56: ```typescript
57: // Instantiate with the chain (and the default hardfork)
58: let c = new Common({ chain: Chain.Ropsten })
59: c.param('gasPrices', 'ecAddGas') // 500
60: 
61: // Chain and hardfork provided
62: c = new Common({ chain: Chain.Ropsten, hardfork: Hardfork.Byzantium })
63: c.param('pow', 'minerReward') // 3000000000000000000
64: 
65: // Get bootstrap nodes for chain/network
66: c.bootstrapNodes() // Array with current nodes
67: 
68: // Instantiate with an EIP activated
69: c = new Common({ chain: Chain.Mainnet, eips: [2537] })
70: ```
71: 
72: # API
73: 
74: ### Docs
75: 
76: See the API documentation for a full list of functions for accessing specific chain and
77: depending hardfork parameters. There are also additional helper functions like
78: `paramByBlock (topic, name, blockNumber)` or `hardforkIsActiveOnBlock (hardfork, blockNumber)`
79: to ease `blockNumber` based access to parameters.
80: 
81: Generated TypeDoc API [Documentation](./docs/README.md)
82: 
83: ### BigInt Support
84: 
85: Starting with v4 the usage of [BN.js](https://github.com/indutny/bn.js/) for big numbers has been removed from the library and replaced with the usage of the native JS [BigInt](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/BigInt) data type (introduced in `ES2020`).
86: 
87: Please note that number-related API signatures have changed along with this version update and the minimal build target has been updated to `ES2020`.
88: 
89: ## Events
90: 
91: The `Common` class is implemented as an `EventEmitter` and is emitting the following events
92: on which you can react within your code:
93: 
94: | Event             | Description                                                |
95: | ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
96: | `hardforkChanged` | Emitted when a hardfork change occurs in the Common object |
97: 
98: ## Setup
99: 
100: ### Chains
101: 
102: The `chain` can be set in the constructor like this:
103: 
104: ```typescript
105: const c = new Common({ chain: Chain.Ropsten })
106: ```
107: 
108: Supported chains:
109: 
110: - `mainnet` (`Chain.Mainnet`)
111: - `ropsten` (`Chain.Ropsten`)
112: - `rinkeby` (`Chain.Rinkeby`)
113: - `goerli` (`Chain.Goerli`)
114: - `sepolia` (`Chain.Sepolia`) (`v2.6.1`+)
115: - Private/custom chain parameters
116: 
117: The following chain-specific parameters are provided:
118: 
119: - `name`
120: - `chainId`
121: - `networkId`
122: - `consensusType` (e.g. `pow` or `poa`)
123: - `consensusAlgorithm` (e.g. `ethash` or `clique`)
124: - `consensusConfig` (depends on `consensusAlgorithm`, e.g. `period` and `epoch` for `clique`)
125: - `genesis` block header values
126: - `hardforks` block numbers
127: - `bootstrapNodes` list
128: - `dnsNetworks` list ([EIP-1459](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1459)-compliant list of DNS networks for peer discovery)
129: 
130: To get an overview of the different parameters have a look at one of the chain-specifc
131: files like `mainnet.json` in the `chains` directory, or to the `Chain` type in [./src/types.ts](./src/types.ts).
132: 
133: ### Working with private/custom chains
134: 
135: There are two distinct APIs available for setting up custom(ized) chains.
136: 
137: #### Basic Chain Customization / Predefined Custom Chains
138: 
139: There is a dedicated `Common.custom()` static constructor which allows for an easy instantiation of a Common instance with somewhat adopted chain parameters, with the main use case to adopt on instantiating with a deviating chain ID (you can use this to adopt other chain parameters as well though). Instantiating a custom common instance with its own chain ID and inheriting all other parameters from `mainnet` can now be as easily done as:
140: 
141: ```typescript
142: const common = Common.custom({ chainId: 1234 })
143: ```
144: 
145: The `custom()` method also takes a string as a first input (instead of a dictionary). This can be used in combination with the `CustomChain` enum dict which allows for the selection of predefined supported custom chains for an easier `Common` setup of these supported chains:
146: 
147: ```typescript
148: const common = Common.custom(CustomChain.ArbitrumRinkebyTestnet)
149: ```
150: 
151: The following custom chains are currently supported:
152: 
153: - `PolygonMainnet`
154: - `PolygonMumbai`
155: - `ArbitrumRinkebyTestnet`
156: - `xDaiChain`
157: - `OptimisticKovan`
158: - `OptimisticEthereum`
159: 
160: `Common` instances created with this simplified `custom()` constructor can't be used in all usage contexts (the HF configuration is very likely not matching the actual chain) but can be useful for specific use cases, e.g. for sending a tx with `@ethereumjs/tx` to an L2 network (see the `Tx` library [README](https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-monorepo/tree/master/packages/tx) for a complete usage example).
161: 
162: #### Activate with a single custom Chain setup
163: 
164: If you want to initialize a `Common` instance with a single custom chain which is then directly activated
165: you can pass a dictionary - conforming to the parameter format described above - with your custom chain
166: values to the constructor using the `chain` parameter or the `setChain()` method, here is some example:
167: 
168: ```typescript
169: import myCustomChain from './[PATH]/myCustomChain.json'
170: const common = new Common({ chain: myCustomChain })
171: ```
172: 
173: #### Initialize using customChains Array
174: 
175: A second way for custom chain initialization is to use the `customChains` constructor option. This
176: option comes with more flexibility and allows for an arbitrary number of custom chains to be initialized on

179: use the `chain` option to activate one of the custom chains passed or activate a build in chain
